De [[pe-normal|la normal]] viene que al: From [[pe-normal|the normal]] comes the fact that on adding noise the variances add; from [[av-edp|the heat equation]], what diffusing means; from [[av-markov|Markov chains]], a process in which each step only looks at the previous one; and from [[av-vectorial|the gradient]], the direction in which something grows fastest. The method that comes out of putting it together is, today, the one that generates almost every image you see about.
[[ia-gan|El GAN]] dejaba un problema: es: [[ia-gan|The GAN]] left a problem: it is a game, and games oscillate. Diffusion changes the strategy completely. Instead of pitting two networks against each other, it defines a forward path that destroys the data little by little, and trains a single network to undo a single step of that path. There is no adversary, no game, and that is why it does not oscillate.
Se coge un dato y se le añade un poco de: You take a datum and add a little normal noise to it. To the result, a little more. And again, a few hundred times, until nothing is left of the original: only noise. Each step is tiny and perfectly known, because we are the ones doing it.

It reads: “x sub t is the square root of one minus beta times x sub t minus one, plus the square root of beta times epsilon”.

The $\beta_t$ is small and says how much noise goes in at that step. The two coefficients are not arbitrary: they are chosen so that the total variance stays at one. If $x_{t-1}$ had variance 1, then $x_t$ has $(1-\beta_t) + \beta_t = 1$. That is why one carries the square root of $1-\beta$ and the other the square root of $\beta$.
And now what makes the method practical. Since adding independent normals gives another normal whose variances add, there is no need to travel the path step by step: you can jump straight to whatever step you want.
el camino de ida entero, de un salto: the whole forward path, in one jump

Where $\overline{\alpha}_t$ is the product of all the $1-\beta$ up to that moment.

This is [[pe-normal|the sum of normals]] applied in a chain, and it is what makes training possible: to show the network step 300 you do not have to simulate 300 steps, it is computed directly. Notice that $\overline{\alpha}_t$ falls from 1 towards 0: at the start almost the whole datum is left, at the end almost only noise.

Esto no es una analogía floja: es la mis: This is not a loose analogy: it is the same equation. Adding normal noise to a variable is equivalent to convolving its density with a bell, and convolving with a widening bell is exactly what [[av-edp|the heat equation's solution]] does.

If you start from a bell of width $\sigma_0$ and let the heat equation act for a time $t$, out comes another bell of width $\sqrt{\sigma_0^2 + 2kt}$. And that is the same as having added normal noise of variance $2kt$.

That is why the data's density gets smoothed as the forward path advances: the peaks flatten and the valleys fill, which is what [[av-edp|there]] the heat did with a bar's temperature.

En [[av-edp|el tema de la ecuación del c: In [[av-edp|the heat equation topic]] there is a pitfall saying that it cannot be rewound: the high modes die down to nearly zero and recovering them would require amplifying any noise enormously. That is still true, and it is not a contradiction with what comes now. A diffusion model does not invert the equation: it does not take a blurry image and compute which sharp one it was. What it does is learn from many examples which data are plausible, and use that to choose a reasonable output among the infinitely many compatible with the noise it receives. That is why two runs give different images: the lost information is not recovered, it is invented plausibly.
Pero ¿no habíamos dicho que el calor no: But hadn't we said that heat does not rewind?

Si no se puede invertir, ¿qué se entrena: If it cannot be inverted, what is trained? Here appears the idea that gives its name to a whole family of methods: instead of learning the data, what is learned is the gradient of the logarithm of their density, which is called the score. In plain words: at each point, which way you would have to move for the datum to be more plausible.
Para una normal $N(\\mu, \\sigma^2)$ sal:
For a normal $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$ out comes a formula you can write from memory: $\log p = -\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2} + \text{const}$, so $s(x) = -\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma^2}$.

Look at what it says: it always points towards the mean, and the harder the further away you are. Following the score is going up the density's slope, that is, moving towards where the data are.

¿Y cómo se aprende el score sin conocer: And how is the score learned without knowing the density? With a lovely trick: the network is asked to guess the noise that was added. Since we made the forward path ourselves, we know exactly what that noise was, so there is a free label for every example. And it turns out that guessing the noise and computing the score are the same thing rescaled.
la pérdida, y por qué equivale al score: the loss, and why it amounts to the score
La primera línea es un error cuadrático: The first line is a bog-standard squared error: it is trained like any other network, with no adversary and no game. The second says that what is learned is the score, divided by how much the noise widened. That is why this is called indifferently a “diffusion model” or a “score-based model”.
Con el score en la mano, generar es empe: With the score in hand, generating is starting at pure noise and taking little steps up the density, undoing one rung at a time. At each step a little new randomness is added, and that is what makes each run give a different result.

Casi todo lo que hoy genera imágenes a p: Almost everything that today generates images from text works like this. Two details change with respect to what you have seen: the noise is removed on a whole image instead of on a number, and for that a network with the structure of [[ia-cnn|a convolutional one]] is used; and for it to obey a sentence the encoded text is also passed to it, so that the learned score is not that of “plausible images” but that of “plausible images given this text”. Many systems, besides, do not diffuse over the pixels but over the compressed code of [[ia-autocodificador|an autoencoder]], which is much cheaper: hence the name latent diffusion.
La idea la publicaron en 2015 Jascha Soh: The idea was published in 2015 by Jascha Sohl-Dickstein, Eric Weiss, Niru Maheswaranathan and Surya Ganguli, explicitly drawing on non-equilibrium thermodynamics: hence the vocabulary of diffusion. For five years it was hardly used. In 2019 Yang Song and Stefano Ermon developed the score-based version, and in 2020 Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain and Pieter Abbeel published the work that made it competitive with GANs in image quality. From there the change was fast: diffusion displaced GANs in image generation in a little over two years, largely because it trains without upsets.
